title: Credit Card Minimum Payment Trap: $5,000 Takes 16 Years
description:
A $5,000 credit card balance at 22% APR. Pay only the minimum and it takes about 16 years and over $7,500 in interest to clear. Pay $300 a month and it's gone in 21 months for about $1,000.

Assumptions: 22% APR (close to the 2026 US average for cards charging interest), minimum payment = 1% of balance + interest with a $35 floor, no new purchases. Minimum-payment formulas vary by card issuer; check your statement. Not financial advice.

#creditcard #personalfinance #debt #moneytips #financialliteracy

scenes.say: Your credit card balance is five thousand dollars. But the minimum payment? Only about a hundred and forty.
The average card that charges interest is now around twenty-two percent a year.
Pay only the minimum, and that five thousand takes sixteen years to clear.
You'd pay over seven and a half thousand dollars in interest. One and a half times what you spent.
Now pay a fixed three hundred a month instead. The debt is gone in under two years.
Total interest? About one thousand dollars, instead of over seven and a half.
The rule is simple. Pay the full balance every month. If you can't, pay as much as you can, and stop using the card until it's clear.

lines.text: Can't? Pay the most you can
